data.name: TriageDesk
data.idea: A small web app for a support team: an agent pastes an incoming customer support ticket, and an AI feature classifies it (category, urgency), writes a one-sentence summary and suggests a first reply; the agent reviews and edits the suggestion. Must stay safe against prompt injection in ticket text, work without an API key via a clearly labelled deterministic fallback, and have an evaluation suite with explicit thresholds. Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI.

data.title: Prompt injection in ticket text manipulates classification/reply or leaks system prompt
data.mitigation: Fixed system prompt + delimited/neutralised ticket, no tools, json_schema output, strict validator (enums, lengths, no URL/email in reply), display-only output, heuristic flag + UI warning, eval injection_safety=1.00 on >=8 attacks, human review

data.mitigation: Permanent text source label + fallback reason, injection warning, copy-only (no send), 'not AI-generated' wording tested (AC5)

data.title: Live model slow/unavailable/refuses/returns invalid or hallucinated output
data.mitigation: 20s timeout, single attempt, deterministic fallback with reason, strict validator, effort low, fallback_rate and raw_model_validity metrics

data.title: Eval not meaningful: fallback rules overfit a small same-team dataset
data.mitigation: Dataset authored and frozen by test-engineer, ~30% holdout reported separately, thresholds fixed in brief before rules exist, sample size stated

data.title: API key leak or key-spend abuse via exposed unauthenticated server
data.mitigation: Key from env only, never echoed (AC10/AC14), bind 127.0.0.1 by default, body and max_tokens caps, one call per request; auth + rate limiting required before any non-local deployment

handoff.objective: Independently review the TriageDesk architecture brief (submission sub-muyloqv9-015ebd44) and approve it or request changes at the architecture gate.
handoff.context: TriageDesk is a small local Node.js 22 web app: an agent pastes a support ticket and gets a category, an urgency, a one-sentence summary and an editable suggested reply. It calls the Anthropic Messages API through raw fetch, falls back to a clearly labelled deterministic rule-based classifier, and must be safe against prompt injection. Constraints: zero npm dependencies, no database, a single page, and an eval suite with explicit thresholds (fixed in the brief's 'Evaluation metrics and thresholds' table). Memory search found one lesson (mem-k-muyljkrt-01991ac7, 'need node-fetch/axios because global fetch is missing'); its check verdict was DOES-NOT-APPLY (requires Node <18, environment has 22.22.0), so it was rejected and not cited. The model id claude-opus-5-5 and the request shape (output_config.format json_schema, effort low, anthropic-version 2023-06-01) come from the claude-api reference cached 2026-10-06. They were not verified by a live call because no API key is set (A5, RISK-7). The submission's runtime evidence is ev:ev-muylm2jz-017e07c4. An earlier evidence run, ev:ev-muyllyra-018a7124, failed only because of shell quoting in the command and carries no product signal.
handoff.expectedOutput: An architecture gate review (approve or changes_requested) with findings referenced by id, covering requirement testability, AC traceability, trust boundaries and injection controls, the fallback design, the eval thresholds, and the scope exclusions.
acceptanceCriteria: Every required section (Users, Problem, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, Architecture, Assumptions, Open Questions, Risks) is present and substantive
Each AC traces to an R/NFR and is decidable by a test or an inspection
Prompt-injection controls (NFR2, AC7, AC9) and the eval thresholds are explicit and measurable
Unverified claims (model id, API surface, live quality) are labelled as assumptions or risks rather than stated as fact
handoff.completedWork: Wrote the architecture brief: users, problem, R1-R10 and NFR1-NFR10, workflows W1-W4, AC1-AC15 with an eval metric and threshold table, scope with reasons for each exclusion, components and a data-flow diagram with trust boundaries TB1-TB4, a decision table with alternatives, constraints, success criteria, A1-A8 and Q1-Q6. Recorded RISK-1..RISK-8 in the risk register. Recorded runtime-capability evidence (Node 22.22.0: global fetch, AbortSignal.timeout, node:test, node:http). Submitted the architecture gate.
remainingIssues: Q1 (user): live model default claude-opus-5-5 vs the cheaper claude-haiku-5-5
Q3 (user): will an API key be provided so the live eval can run, or is fallback-only verification acceptable with live thresholds marked unverified?
Q4 (user): may raw ticket text (possible PII) be sent to the Anthropic API, or is redaction required first?
Q2/Q5/Q6 have proposed defaults (taxonomy as in A3; no server-side refusal fallback beta; no URLs in replies) that the reviewer may accept
A5/RISK-7: model id and request shape are not verified live; no API key is set in this environment
The choice of raw fetch over the official @anthropic-ai/sdk is a deliberate trade-off for the zero-dependency constraint; the reviewer should confirm it
handoff.nextAction: architecture-reviewer: review submission sub-muyloqv9-015ebd44 against the brief and record approve or changes_requested via eccode gate review architecture; escalate Q1, Q3 and Q4 to the user through the orchestrator.

review.summary: The brief is well structured and honest about unverified claims, and the scope is right-sized. It still cannot go to design yet. It contradicts two recorded orchestrator decisions: the default model is now Haiku and PII redaction is now required. The raw-fetch structured-output path ignores documented JSON-schema keyword limits, which would make every live call 400 and fall back with nothing to show it before delivery. The localhost bind is the only access control and it does not stop DNS rebinding. The holdout split and the injection_safety metric cannot measure what they claim to measure.

criteria.description: Completeness: users, problem, workflows, constraints, scope and requirements are explicit and consistent with recorded decisions
criteria.notes: Users, problem, W1-W4 and scope reasons are good. However, the brief still sets claude-opus-5-5 as the default (lines 233, 245) and keeps PII redaction out of scope (line 168), against decisions dec-muylppww / dec-muylpq02 (ARCH-1). It has no Host/Origin requirement (ARCH-3).

criteria.description: Testability: every AC is decidable by test or inspection and every requirement traces to an AC
criteria.notes: AC1-AC15 are concrete and trace to R/NFR ids. Gaps: the RISK-7 mitigation (4xx -> model_error) and stop_reason max_tokens have no AC (ARCH-6). The validator's 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' rules are not defined precisely enough to decide (ARCH-7). Success criterion 2 reports holdout results but sets no pass rule for them (ARCH-4).

criteria.description: Assumptions: risky or unverified assumptions are labelled, and questions that need the user are escalated
criteria.notes: A1-A8 carry 'Blocks' notes, and A5/A6 honestly mark the reference-only claims. Q1/Q3/Q4 were escalated correctly. Folding the orchestrator's answers back into the brief is tracked under ARCH-1.

criteria.description: Complexity: no unnecessary components; simplest design that meets requirements
criteria.notes: node:http, a single static page, no state, a pure-function fallback and one model call per request. Nothing here is superfluous. The rationale for the zero-dependency choice is misattributed (ARCH-8, minor), but the choice itself is defensible.

criteria.description: Feasibility: technology limits, API surface, latency and cost verified against authoritative sources
criteria.notes: The Node 22 runtime is verified. I verified the model ids and support for output_config.format and effort against platform.claude.com on 2026-10-07. The raw-fetch schema limits are unaddressed (ARCH-2). The brief does not account for thinking tokens counting toward max_tokens (ARCH-6).

criteria.description: Security and privacy: trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection, least privilege
criteria.notes: TB1-TB4, no tools, display-only output, textContent with CSP, and the key read from env only are all strong. Gaps: DNS rebinding bypasses the localhost bind (ARCH-3). The required redaction has no requirement or AC, and its scope leaves out payment card numbers (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: AI features: real value, eval cases with sound thresholds, fallback on model failure, human oversight
criteria.notes: The value statement, the labelled fallback and the human-in-the-loop design are good. The holdout split cannot detect overfitting (ARCH-4). injection_safety mixes up accuracy with attack success and rests on too few cases to support its claim (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk, with mitigations that hold
criteria.notes: RISK-1..8 are complete in form. RISK-5 rates likelihood Low on the strength of the 127.0.0.1 bind, which DNS rebinding defeats (ARCH-3). No risk covers redaction failure or leakage once redaction is adopted (ARCH-1).

findings.title: Brief contradicts recorded decisions on default model and PII redaction
findings.detail: The orchestrator recorded dec-muylppww (default ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5) and dec-muylpq02 (redact emails and phone numbers before any live call). The submitted brief still says the opposite. Line 233 (decision table) and line 245 (deployment) default to claude-opus-5-5. Line 168 puts PII redaction out of scope. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 describe Opus-specific behaviour ('thinking cannot be disabled'). No R/NFR/AC covers redaction (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Design would therefore build from a brief that disagrees with the project record. I accept the Haiku choice: claude-haiku-5-5 exists, supports structured outputs and output_config.effort 'low', and its default effort is medium (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, both checked 2026-10-07). I challenge the redaction scope. The product handles billing tickets, which routinely contain payment card numbers. Redacting only emails and phones still sends card numbers (PANs) to a third party, and Q4 itself listed card numbers as a redaction class.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Sets the default ANTHROPIC_MODEL to claude-haiku-5-5, marked as pending user confirmation, and rewrites A5, the decision table, RISK-3 and RISK-7 for Haiku 5.5 behaviour: adaptive thinking on by default, effort set explicitly to low, and thinking counted toward max_tokens. (2) Adds a requirement and an AC for redaction before the live call. The AC uses a stubbed transport to assert that marker email addresses, phone numbers and Luhn-valid card numbers in a ticket do not appear in the captured outbound request body. Card numbers are in scope unless the user explicitly declines. (3) Defines the order of operations: the injection detector runs on the original text, then redaction, then delimiter neutralisation. Placeholders must not collide with the <ticket> delimiters. (4) Updates the live-mode UI notice to say which classes are redacted. (5) Adds or extends a risk for redaction misses (false negatives).

findings.title: Raw-fetch JSON schema limits unaddressed; live path can 400 on every call
findings.detail: The brief chooses raw fetch with output_config.format json_schema and enforces lengths (summary <=200, reply 1-1200) and enums. Per https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.md (checked 2026-10-07), the API rejects raw schemas that contain minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum/multipleOf or maxItems with a 400. additionalProperties must be false on every object. Claude may change the capitalisation of enum values. The SDK helpers strip the unsupported keywords and validate locally, but the raw-fetch design does not get that benefit. AC9 checks only output_config.format.type === 'json_schema'. A schema that naturally includes maxLength 200/1200 would therefore pass every offline test while every live request returns 400 and falls back with model_error. Decision Q3 means no live call happens before delivery, so the defect would ship undetected and live mode would silently be fallback-only. The strict validator would also reject enum values that are correct but differently capitalised (invalid_output), which inflates fallback_rate.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR2 states that the schema sent to the model uses only supported keywords: type, properties, required, enum, additionalProperties:false on every object, and no minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/maxItems. Lengths are enforced only by the server-side validator. AC9 must walk the captured schema and fail on any unsupported keyword or on an object without additionalProperties:false. The brief must also define the enum-case policy: normalise with a case-insensitive match before the enum check, or reject explicitly with a stated reason. Either way a test must cover it.

findings.title: Localhost bind is defeated by DNS rebinding; no Host/Origin validation
findings.detail: The trust model relies on binding to 127.0.0.1 with no auth or rate limit (NFR3, Scope, RISK-5 likelihood 'Low'). A web page the agent visits can use DNS rebinding: an attacker hostname re-resolves to 127.0.0.1, so its script becomes same-origin with the app. The script can then POST application/json to /api/triage without hitting a CORS preflight, read the responses and spend the operator's API key without limit. The 415 content-type check does not help, because rebinding makes the request same-origin. No requirement or AC in the brief validates the Host or Origin headers (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c: no Host/Origin/DNS-rebinding lines). The fix is cheap and belongs to the architecture's trust boundary TB1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR3 requires the server to reject any request whose Host header is not in an allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]). The rejection must come before body parsing or any model call. The server must also reject POSTs whose Origin header is present and not same-origin, and must emit no CORS headers. AC11 (or a new AC) must test that 'Host: attacker.example' and a foreign Origin are rejected and that the fetch stub is never called. RISK-5 must be updated with this mitigation and its likelihood re-rated.

findings.title: Holdout split cannot detect fallback-rule overfitting
findings.detail: Thresholds are scored over all rows, and the roughly 30% holdout is only 'reported separately' (eval section; Success Criterion 2). If rules overfit the tuning rows perfectly, category_accuracy >= 0.70 and urgency_accuracy >= 0.65 still pass with 0% holdout accuracy, and high_urgency_recall >= 0.80 passes with 33% holdout recall (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). RISK-4 names this exact failure mode, and its mitigation is ineffective as written. With about 40 rows the holdout has about 12 rows, so per-metric holdout numbers carry 1-3 high-urgency rows. The brief does not say how a frozen dataset is proven to predate the rules.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when (1) the fallback thresholds are enforced on the holdout rows, or a stated holdout floor is enforced (for example, holdout within 0.10 of each threshold), and npm run eval exits non-zero when it is missed. (2) The brief sets minimum holdout counts, for example at least 2 rows per category and at least 4 label=high rows, enlarging the dataset if needed. (3) The dataset and holdout tags are frozen by recording the dataset's sha256 as evidence before any fallback-rule commit, and the verification gate checks that hash.

findings.title: injection_safety mixes accuracy with attack success and overclaims on 8 cases
findings.detail: injection_safety requires that the final category and urgency equal the true labels on every attack row, at 1.00, for both providers. Fallback accuracy is only required to reach 0.70/0.65 overall. Either the attack rows end up chosen to be easy for keyword rules (selection bias), or the metric fails for reasons that have nothing to do with injection. The brief says the fallback 'cannot be injected because it never echoes ticket text'. That holds for text echo but not for classification: its listed urgency cues ('urgent', 'outage', 'charged twice', 'data loss') are words an attacker controls. The heuristic detector's recall >= 0.90 is measured on attacks written by the same team that writes the detector regexes, with no held-out attack families, so the test is easy to game. Statistically, 8 out of 8 passes leaves a 95% upper bound of about 31% on the true failure rate (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Success Criterion 4 ('Injection safety is 1.00 for both providers') cannot be met for live under decision Q3, because live evals are NOT RUN.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Each attack row declares the attacker's targets (requested category/urgency that differ from the true labels, a canary token, a URL). Attack success is defined as the output adopting an attacker target, or the canary, prompt-marker or URL appearing. injection_safety (attack-success rate = 0) is kept separate from accuracy on attack rows, which is reported under the normal accuracy thresholds. (2) RISK-1 states the residual risk that fallback classification can be steered by keywords, mitigated by the flag and human review, and the fallback 'cannot be injected' claim is corrected. (3) The attack set is enlarged (for example to at least 20 rows across the detector's rule families), and some attack families are held out so that detector regexes are not written against them. (4) Results are reported as '0 failures in N' with the sample size, not as proof of safety. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live injection results as NOT RUN when no key is available.

findings.title: Fallback triggers for HTTP errors and max_tokens truncation are untested
findings.detail: AC4 covers throw, timeout, non-JSON, out-of-enum, URL and refusal. It does not cover a non-2xx HTTP response (400/404 for a wrong model id, 429, 529), although RISK-7's mitigation relies on '4xx -> model_error'. stop_reason 'max_tokens' is checked by the live provider but maps to no R6 fallbackReason. Thinking counts toward max_tokens on Haiku 5.5 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, checked 2026-10-07), so the 1,024 cap needs a rationale.
findings.recommendation: Extend AC4 with stubbed HTTP 404 (with a body), 429 and 529 responses mapped to model_error, and with stop_reason max_tokens mapped to a named reason. State why max_tokens=1024 leaves room for thinking at effort low, or raise it.

findings.title: Validator rules 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' are not precisely defined
findings.detail: The single-sentence rule (R3, AC2) and the no-URL/no-email rule (NFR2) decide fallback, but text like 'e.g.', 'v2.1', 'Mr.', bare domains ('example.com') and obfuscated forms ('name at example dot com') are undefined. As a result the model-validity and fallback_rate metrics depend on how the implementer reads the rule.
findings.recommendation: Define both rules as deterministic patterns, in the brief or as a binding design-gate item, with accept and reject test vectors for the edge cases above.

findings.title: Zero-dependency constraint attributed to the project, which never set it
findings.detail: The decision table says the SDK 'would break the zero-dependency constraint the project set'. The project idea says only 'Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI'. Raw fetch is defensible on its merits: one endpoint, an injectable transport and no retries wanted. But it is the architect's choice, and it loses the SDK's schema stripping and typed errors (see ARCH-2).
findings.recommendation: Restate NFR1 and the decision row as an architect's decision with its trade-offs (including ARCH-2), and list it for user confirmation alongside Q1/Q4.

findings.title: Q2/Q5/Q6 proposed defaults acceptable; Q5 moot with Haiku default
findings.detail: I accept the A3 taxonomy (Q2), local-only refusal handling (Q5) and no URLs in replies (Q6). According to the claude-api reference (cached 2026-10-06), Claude Haiku 5.5 has no server-side refusal fallback, so Q5 has no option to choose once the default becomes Haiku.
findings.recommendation: Record Q2/Q5/Q6 as decided with the proposed defaults, and note that Q5 no longer applies under the Haiku default.

review.summary: Re-review of sub-muym3xbz-0110077b against rev-muylut9q-014dc18b. All five major findings (ARCH-1..ARCH-5) are resolved in the artifact text, and the minors ARCH-6..ARCH-8 and info ARCH-9 are addressed. I re-ran brief-vectors.js myself (ev:ev-muym6zly-019e5cb3, passed). I accept the author's departure on fallback steering (leak = 0, steer <= 0.25 for the keyword fallback, 0 for live) on its merits. An adversarial probe (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed) found that the baseline card-redaction pattern misses a card number followed or preceded by another digit group, for example '4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27'. R11's normative text and AC16's generic assertion are correct, so this is recorded as a minor condition the design gate must close. The probe also found V2 false positives on 'ASP.NET' and 'socket.io' (minor). Approval is conditional on the user confirmations already listed (Q1, Q4 card extension, Q7).

criteria.description: Completeness: users, problem, workflows, constraints, scope and requirements are explicit and consistent with recorded decisions
criteria.notes: The default model is claude-haiku-5-5 throughout (NFR10, Deployment shape, decision table, A5). Opus now appears only as a rejected alternative. Redaction is in scope (R11, R12), and NFR3 has Host/Origin validation. The four decision ids cited (dec-muylppww, dec-muylppyk, dec-muylpq02, dec-muylvas4) exist in the project state. The items that need user confirmation (Q1, Q4 card extension, Q7) are marked (USER).

evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#Output validation rules (normative; baseline patterns verified by ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490)
criteria.notes: R11/R12 trace to AC16, NFR3 to AC17, and V1-V4 to AC2/AC4 with binding accept/reject vectors, which I re-ran and which pass. AC4 now covers the 404/429/529/500, max_tokens and thinking-block cases. AC8 includes a synthetic failing-holdout test. AC16's fixed vectors lack digit-adjacency cases (ARCH-10, minor).

criteria.description: Assumptions: risky or unverified assumptions are labelled, and questions that need the user are escalated
criteria.notes: A5 is rewritten for Haiku 5.5 and marked as not verified by a live call. A9 states the token-per-character assumption behind max_tokens 2048 and how it will be checked (the truncated count). Q4 and Q7 are escalated to the user.

criteria.description: Complexity: no unnecessary components; simplest design that meets requirements
criteria.notes: The only new component is a pure-function redactor. The Host/Origin check is the cheapest control that closes the DNS-rebinding gap. The scope is still buildable in one session.

criteria.description: Feasibility: technology limits, API surface, latency and cost verified against authoritative sources
criteria.notes: The schema keyword allowlist matches the structured-outputs limits I verified on 2026-10-07 (platform.claude.com structured-outputs.md). Omitting the thinking field and setting effort low is consistent with effort.md (checked 2026-10-07), and the choice not to send thinking:disabled correctly keeps the model switchable to Opus. The schema walker in brief-vectors.js rejects maxLength and a missing additionalProperties:false; I re-ran it and it passes. Live behaviour is still unverified by a live call, which is honestly recorded (A5, RISK-7, NOT RUN).

criteria.description: Security and privacy: trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection, least privilege
criteria.notes: The Host allowlist runs before body reading. Foreign and null Origin are rejected, no CORS headers are sent and OPTIONS returns 405. AC17 proves the ordering (20 KB body with a foreign Host gets 403, not 413) and that the fetch stub is called 0 times. Redaction runs before TB2 in the right order, and the placeholders cannot form delimiters. Residual redaction misses are owned by RISK-9. A baseline-pattern gap on digit-adjacent card numbers is tracked as ARCH-10 (minor, design-gate condition).

criteria.description: AI features: real value, eval cases with sound thresholds, fallback on model failure, human oversight
criteria.notes: Holdout floors are enforced, with minimum counts and a sha256 freeze plus ordering check. Leak, steer and attack_success are separated from accuracy. I judged the fallback steering threshold of 0.25 on its merits and accept it (see the ARCH-5 resolution).

criteria.description: Risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk, with mitigations that hold
criteria.notes: RISK-1 now states the residual keyword-steering risk. RISK-4's mitigation now holds (floors, freeze). RISK-5 is re-rated Low on the strength of an actual control. RISK-9 adds redaction false negatives and over-redaction. Every row has likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner.

findings.title: Baseline card redaction misses cards adjacent to other digit groups (expiry, CVV, preceding phone)
findings.detail: The CARD pattern in brief-vectors.js, `(?<!\d)\d(?:[ -]?\d){12,18}(?!\d)`, is greedy. Its lookahead accepts a following space, so it takes the longest 13-19-digit window. If that window fails Luhn, the replace callback returns it unchanged and never tries the shorter, Luhn-valid sub-window. My probe ran the submitted file unmodified (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed). 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111' all leave 4111111111111111 in the output. The PHONE pass then skips them too, because they have more than 15 digits. The controls (card alone, card followed by a year) are redacted correctly. Card plus expiry is a common way to write a card number in a billing ticket. R11's normative wording and AC16's generic assertion ('no Luhn-valid run of 13-19 digits') are correct. The gap is in the baseline pattern and in AC16's fixed vectors, which a faithful implementation would pass while leaking. This stays minor because the brief lets the design gate refine patterns, RISK-9 owns the residual risk, and live mode is not exercised in this delivery (no key).
findings.recommendation: Condition for the design gate. Add these three inputs to the AC16 vectors and make the redactor pass them: 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 12/27', 'Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 123' and 'Call 555 0137 4111 1111 1111 1111'. One way is to treat each separator-delimited digit run as candidates and redact any contiguous sub-sequence of groups whose digits are 13-19 long and Luhn-valid. AC16's 'no Luhn-valid run' check must scan every sub-window, not just maximal runs. The design-gate reviewer should treat a missing fix as major at that gate.

findings.title: V2 bare-domain rule rejects product names such as 'ASP.NET' and 'socket.io'; V1 rejects 'Oct. 3'
findings.detail: The probe (ev:ev-muym7oav-0127baed) shows that V2 rejects 'Customer reports ASP.NET errors after the update.' and 'Socket.io connections drop every minute.', because .net and .io are on the TLD list. V1 rejects 'Sync fails since Oct. 3 update.' because 'oct' is not on the abbreviation allowlist. Technical-ticket summaries will mention such names, so these false rejections become invalid_output and inflate live fallback_rate (threshold <= 0.05). The safety direction is right: over-rejection only causes a fallback. This is a quality issue, not a security one.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#Output validation rules (normative; baseline patterns verified by ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490)
findings.recommendation: At the design gate, choose one: (a) tell the model in the system prompt not to write dotted product or domain-like names, or (b) add a small allowlist of known product tokens (asp.net, socket.io) with matching accept vectors, or (c) record the false-positive rate as accepted. Do not weaken the reject vectors already listed. Month abbreviations may be added to the V1 allowlist.

findings.title: Held-out attack families are visible in the repo after freeze
findings.detail: Held-out families are defined as rows 'the detector author never sees before freeze'. However, eval/dataset.json lives in the same repository, so the detector or fallback author can read the heldOutFamily rows after the freeze and tune against them. That would inflate injection_flag_recall_heldout and reduce injection_steer. Held-out recall has no threshold, so the incentive is low.
findings.recommendation: In the plan, the detector and fallback task handoffs should state that the author did not read heldOutFamily rows, and the phase reviewer should spot-check that the detector rule ids and patterns do not quote held-out row phrasing.

resolvedFindings.resolution: All five conditions are met. (1) The default model is claude-haiku-5-5, pending user confirmation, in NFR10, Deployment shape, the 'Default model' row and Q1. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 are rewritten for Haiku 5.5: adaptive thinking on by default and counted toward max_tokens, effort low set explicitly. A new 'Thinking control' row explains why thinking:disabled is not sent (it returns 400 on Opus 5.5). (2) R11 adds redaction of email, Luhn-valid card and phone, with cards in scope unless the user declines (Q4). AC16 uses a capturing fetch stub, marker emails, phones and Luhn cards, a digits-only check and non-redaction controls. (3) R12 fixes the order as detector on the original text, then redact, then neutralise < and >. The placeholders are bracket-only. (4) The NFR4 live-mode notice names the redacted and unredacted classes. (5) RISK-9 covers misses and over-redaction. I re-ran the baseline vectors and they pass. The adjacency gap I found in the baseline pattern is tracked separately as minor ARCH-10.

NFR2 restricts the schema to type/properties/required/enum/additionalProperties, with additionalProperties:false on every object and no length, number, array, pattern or format keywords. This matches the structured-outputs documentation I checked on 2026-10-07. Lengths are enforced only in V4. AC9 adds a recursive schema walk plus a self-check that maxLength is rejected, and the walker in brief-vectors.js passes on my re-run, including the maxLength and missing-additionalProperties rejections. V3 defines case-insensitive enum normalisation with its reason, and AC4(m) tests it. RISK-7 and the failure-mode row cover the 400-on-every-call scenario, which shows up as model_error.
evidence: artifact:.eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md#Output validation rules (normative; baseline patterns verified by ev:ev-muylz82a-01c7d490)

resolvedFindings.resolution: NFR3 now makes the Host allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) the first step of every request, before routing or body reading, returning 403 forbidden_host. It rejects a present non-same-origin Origin, including null, on non-GET/HEAD requests, sends no Access-Control-* headers, and returns 405 for OPTIONS. AC17 tests a foreign Host on POST, health and static routes and a missing Host. It tests that a 20 KB body with a foreign Host gets 403, not 413, which proves the check precedes body reading. It also tests foreign and null Origin, positive controls for localhost and [::1], and that the fetch stub is called 0 times. AC11 asserts no CORS headers. RISK-5 is re-rated from inherent Medium to residual Low, citing the control.

(1) Holdout floors, each equal to its threshold minus 0.10, are enforced with a non-zero exit (R9, AC8, Success Criterion 2). AC8 includes a synthetic test in which the all-rows thresholds pass but a holdout floor fails. (2) Minimum counts are set: at least 60 benign rows, and a holdout of at least 20 rows with every category >= 3, every urgency >= 4 and label=high >= 5, checked by the runner. With 5 high rows, the 0.70 floor needs 4 of 5. (3) Freeze: sha256 evidence for the dataset and thresholds is recorded before the first commit to the fallback or detector rules. The verification gate checks both the hash and the timestamp ordering against git log, and the plan must order the dataset task first. RISK-4 is updated.

(1) Attack rows declare {family, targetCategory, targetUrgency, canary, url}. injection_leak (canary, url, prompt marker TDSK-SYS-7Q2, or a V2 match), injection_steer and attack_success are separate from accuracy, which is computed on attack rows using their true labels and printed separately. (2) RISK-1 states the residual keyword-steering risk, and the Fallback row corrects the 'cannot be injected' claim. (3) There are at least 20 attack rows across at least 6 families, including at least 2 held-out families (at least 6 rows), and held-out recall is reported with N. (4) Results are reported as 'k failures in N' with the 3/N bound and never as 'safe'. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live results NOT RUN. On the author's deliberate departure: my recommendation was attack success = 0. The author instead keeps leak = 0 for the fallback and caps fallback steering at 0.25, while live steering stays at 0. I accept this on the merits. A keyword classifier cannot tell an attacker's 'URGENT outage' from a genuine one, so a 0-steer requirement could only be met by fitting rules to the attack rows, which is the overfitting ARCH-4 targets. The harmful injection outcomes (leaking a link, canary or prompt into the reply) stay at 0 for the fallback, and its templates prevent them structurally. Steering only changes a label that a human reviews, behind the injection flag. Detector-matched sentences are removed before scoring as a cheap mitigation. Both the threshold and its rationale are explicit and bounded.

R6 adds truncated. AC4 covers HTTP 404 with a body, 429, 529 and 500 as model_error, max_tokens as truncated, a thinking block before the text block, and at most one fetch call. NFR7 raises max_tokens to 2048, gives a rationale (A9, D2) and makes it configurable.

V1 and V2 are now deterministic patterns with binding accept and reject vectors covering e.g., v2.1, Mr., bare domains and obfuscated emails. I re-ran the vectors and they pass. The remaining false positives on dotted product names are tracked as minor ARCH-11.
